children: Most Gulf equity markets fell on Sunday as flare-ups across the Middle East rattled sentiment and triggered a broad market retreat.
dropped 2%, dragged down by a 2.5% slide in Al Rajhi Bank
and a 2.2% fall in the country's biggest lender by assets, Saudi National Bank

Saudi-led forces downed a missile aimed by the Iran-aligned Houthis at the west of the kingdom early on Sunday, while Iran's army said its air defence fired on and damaged a US F-16 over Gulf waters on Friday, an account denied by the United States.
A Qatari delegation held talks in Tehran on Friday night, an Iranian official said, as diplomats push to end the war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February.
Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran still hopes diplomacy can prevail, although US President Donald Trump said that while Iran wants a deal, it is not one he will accept.
fell 1.6%, with almost all of its constituent shares in negative territory, including Qatar Islamic Bank

The weekend attacks added to pressure from last week's global market selloff, said Milad Azar, market analyst at XTB MENA, with banks leading declines in both Saudi Arabia and Qatar and heavyweight stocks taking the biggest hit.
fell 3.2%, with Azar saying that gold's fall to a more than one-year low had hurt its mining outlook.
"However, losses in Saudi Arabia were partly contained as oil prices held broadly steady, limiting pressure on Saudi Aramco and other energy-linked shares," he said.

Bahrain said it had intercepted Iranian aerial attacks in recent days, with one sparking a fire at a civilian industrial facility. The Revolutionary Guards said they targeted US military positions in the kingdom, home to the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. Gulf Arab states have come under repeated fire from Tehran since the war broke out.
